Outbreak of Respiratory Illness Disrupts Belarusian Steel Production

A sudden outbreak of acute respiratory illness among steelworkers in Belarus is causing significant disruption to the nation’s steel industry, industry officials confirmed on Thursday. The disease, which health authorities say is likely a highly contagious viral infection, has led to a wave of worker absences and forced several steel plants to scale back or temporarily halt operations.

According to the Belarusian Metallurgical Industry Association, at least 600 workers have reported symptoms over the past week, with many requiring hospitalization. The hardest hit sites include the sprawling Novomir Steel Works outside Gomel and the Byelorussian Steel Foundry in Mogilev, both of which have reduced output by nearly 40% since Monday. The association said that additional facilities are operating with skeleton crews as management tries to contain the outbreak.

“Production has been severely affected. With so many workers ill or quarantined, we are unable to maintain normal output levels,” said Sergei Ivanovich, spokesperson for Novomir Steel Works. “Our priority is the health and safety of our employees, but the financial impact on the industry is already significant.”

Analysts estimate that Belarus’s steel output could fall by as much as 28% this month if the situation does not improve. “Steel is a major export for Belarus and any prolonged disruption could have lasting repercussions for the sector’s competitiveness,” said Natalia Kovalchuk, an independent industry analyst based in Minsk.

Union representatives have called for stricter health protocols and urgent government assistance. “We urge immediate action to safeguard workers and mitigate the economic fallout,” said Pavel Rudakov, head of the Belarusian Steelworkers Union.

Health authorities are continuing to investigate the source of the outbreak and have implemented expanded testing at all major steel sites. The situation remains fluid, with no clear timeline for a return to full production.
